articles.title: Israel likely to lose Gaza genocide case if ICJ follows Myanmar ruling, Tel Aviv scholar says
articles.summary:
Israel likely to lose Gaza genocide case if ICJ follows Myanmar ruling, Tel Aviv scholar says

Israel will probably lose the genocide case brought by South Africa if the International Court of Justice (ICJ) applies the reasoning it used last week to find Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, an Israeli international law scholar has said.

“It is very bad that we have reached this point. It is a real earthquake,” said Eliav Lieblich, a professor at Tel Aviv University’s law faculty.

“Before jumping to conspiracy theories about the court, Israel has mainly itself to blame,” he wrote in a series of posts in Hebrew on X. “Even if you disagree with the majority on every legal point, no reasonable country should come anywhere close to falling short of the standards it set. In many respects, Netanyahu’s government dug this hole itself.”

The ICJ on Thursday concluded in a 9-6 decision that Myanmar's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya population in northern Rakhine State during the military's 2017 operations.

The judgment, the first time the UN's highest court has found a state responsible for genocide, offers South Africa a significant legal precedent in its case accusing Israel of committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, particularly over how judges assess genocidal intent when a state claims its military actions are driven by security objectives.

Read more: Israel likely to lose Gaza genocide case if ICJ follows Myanmar ruling, Tel Aviv scholar says

articles.title: Iran vows to use 'all avaliable tools' to confront US naval blockade
articles.summary:
Iran vows to use 'all avaliable tools' to confront US naval blockade

Iran has warned the US against its naval blockade of Iranian oil exports, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei saying Tehran would not tolerate the "American aggression".

“We will use all the means at our disposal to counter US aggression,” Baqaei said on Monday.

The blockade, first imposed in April and halted in June, was reinstated in July after a memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran collapsed.

This warning comes as the two countries continue to exchange accusations over attacks in the Gulf. Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, while the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps said they had launched missiles and drones on US ‌military positions in the country.
